sessions.prompt:
Add normalize_phone(s) to phones.py: spaces are removed ("+31 6 1234 5678" becomes "+31612345678"). Add tests.

The plan for normalize_phone has one more step: dashes, dots and brackets are removed too ("+31 (6) 12-34.56" becomes "+316123456"). Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): an email address must have exactly one "@", some text before it, and a dot in the text after it: any function given another email raises ValueError.

Design decision for this project: a phone number that starts with 0 is a local number: normalize_phone replaces the 0 with the default country code +31.

given.handoff: Session 1 added normalize_phone(s) with tests. Its last step is left for later: remove dashes, dots and brackets.
decisions: An email needs exactly one @, text before it and a dot after it; another raises ValueError in any function.
A phone number starting with 0 gets the default country code +31 in place of the 0.

sessions.prompt:
Add an AddressBook class to book.py: add(name, phone=None, email=None) adds a contact, get(name) returns a dict with the keys name, phone and email (None when missing; the phone is normalized), and names() returns the contact names. Add tests.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): names are stored with each word capitalized ("ann van zed" becomes "Ann Van Zed"), in every function.

Design decision for this project: names() is sorted by last name.

Design decision for this project: the header line of a CSV export is name,phone,email.

given.handoff: Session 2 added AddressBook.add, get and names with tests.
decisions: Names are stored with each word capitalized, in every function.
names() is sorted by last name.
The CSV export header is name,phone,email.

sessions.prompt:
Add AddressBook.remove(name) to book.py. Add tests.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): names() is sorted by first name, not last name.

Design decision for this project: adding a contact whose name is already in the book raises ValueError; names ignore case in that check.

Design decision for this project: a contact needs a phone or an email: adding one with neither raises ValueError.

decisions: Supersedes last name: names() is sorted by first name.
Adding a name already in the book raises ValueError (ignoring case).
A contact needs a phone or an email; neither raises ValueError.

sessions.prompt:
Add AddressBook.search(text) to book.py: the sorted names that contain text, ignoring case. Add tests.

The plan for AddressBook.search has one more step: it also matches contacts whose email contains text. Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): the default country code for local numbers is +49, not +31.

given.handoff: Session 4 added AddressBook.search(text) with tests. Its last step is left for later: also match emails.
decisions: Supersedes +31: the default country code for local numbers is +49.

sessions.prompt:

The plan for initials has one more step: each part of a hyphenated name counts as a word ("Mary-Jane Lee" gives "MJL"). Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

given.handoff: Session 5 added initials(name) with tests. Its last step is left for later: hyphenated parts count as words.

sessions.prompt:
Add AddressBook.count() to book.py. Add tests.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): the header line of a CSV export is name,email,phone, not name,phone,email.

Design decision for this project: in a CSV export a missing phone or email is an empty field.

Design decision for this project: the last line of a CSV export is the number of contacts, in the form # 3 contacts.

decisions: Supersedes name,phone,email: the CSV export header is name,email,phone.
In a CSV export a missing phone or email is an empty field.
The last CSV export line is # 3 contacts.
